style_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the dark storm look (D19) and the dark base (D9). Borrow Apple's zoom gating and labels, not its light cream base. Recommended for these reasons; not a ranking.
reasons: D19 kept the dark storm design and set aside the handoff's off-white/navy/teal (docs/DECISIONS.md:129-134).

D9 draws the base dark by CSS invert of USGS tiles (docs/DECISIONS.md:66-69). Apple's land #F7F7EF covers 26-41% of each frame; a light base would be the brightest area under radar and cloud layers (design reasoning; storm palette not measured).
Tokens (templates/base.html:13-16) give text #e9f0f7 at 15.84:1 on #0c1622; muted #8ea6bf 7.24:1; wheat #e0a93c 8.59:1.
The owner's own nav bar #1E293B is 5.4 RGB units from granite #1C2C3F, so only the map area is light in the owner's UI.
Copy Apple's zoom gating, not its colours: landmark pins at 11.6; venues at 14.0; full POIs and street names at 15-16.

extractor_integration.what_it_is: Owner's iOS app; subtitle 'Tap map to add 5 points (Apple Maps / MapKit)'. No extractor code, export sample or spec is in this repo; export format and OSM selection rule are unverified.
extractor_integration.current_intake: Territories are GeoJSON text rows (payload/store.py:33-34; add_territory store.py:195-196), created only via the drawn-shape form and wx.clean_polygon (payload/app.py:556-572).
extractor_integration.clean_polygon_limits: weather.py:351-375: type Polygon only; rings[0] only (holes dropped silently); 4-5,000 outer vertices.
extractor_integration.matching_already_handles: weather.py:262 _polygons and point_in handle MultiPolygon and holes; territories match at app.py:296 and :307; D10 adds zone geometry; unknown shows Can't tell yet.

entry_paths.how: one outer ring as GeoJSON Polygon, no holes, 5,000 vertices or fewer, via the existing form
entry_paths.limits: holes lost; MultiPolygon refused; big admin outlines may exceed 5,000 vertices

entry_paths.how: extend clean_polygon to accept MultiPolygon and keep holes; add a GeoJSON import form
entry_paths.code_change: payload change; ships on manifest version bump (AGENTS.md rule 1); tests

entry_paths.how: simplify to 5,000 vertices or fewer with a documented tolerance before import
entry_paths.limits: boundary changes; UI must say so

extractor_integration.alert_rules: Rule 6 and D10: match by polygon or zone geometry; a rejected import must say why, never match nothing silently.
extractor_integration.licence: OSM data is ODbL with attribution; the app already credits OSM for Nominatim results (payload/app.py:875-878). A boundary shipped inside payload/ reaches every install; share-alike duties need a licence review.
extractor_integration.osm_use_in_app: Nominatim only (weather.py:1087, 1112). Tile policy bans bulk prefetch and offline use, so OSM tiles could not serve the offline self-test.

open_questions: Extractor export: GeoJSON Feature or FeatureCollection? Polygon or MultiPolygon? Holes kept? Needs a sample before importer design.
Selection rule: which OSM object do five taps pick (admin boundary containing all taps, smallest, nearest; admin_level)? Store the OSM relation id and timestamp.
Licence: is one extracted boundary inside payload/ a Produced Work or a derived database with share-alike duties? Needs review before it ships.

Apple screenshots: the terms restrict copying any portion of the Service (s1.3(vi)); the owner decides whether the six copies stay in the repo before any push; confirm nothing under payload/ references them.
Zoom gaps: nothing between 5.4 and 11.6, none above 16.0; a zoom 8-9 and a zoom 17 frame would complete the set.
POIs and district layers: none in README s3; choose a self-hosted OSM extract (ODbL, no bulk tile use) or leave them out.
3D buildings: choose a footprint source with a compatible licence first; Google 3D Tiles are paid and not cacheable (README s2 D-G4).
USGS per-layer credits: some non-USGS images are copyrighted; check each National Map layer before publishing.
limits: Zoom assumes 402 pt at 3 px per point (device not named): a 2x scale adds 0.58 to every zoom; a 512-pt tile convention subtracts 1. Neither was checked against Apple documentation.

Error about +/-0.2 from pin placement (Apple pins vs OSM centroids differ by tens of metres; parks worst). Spreads: region 5.377-5.384; valley 11.58-11.75; city 13.91-14.19; downtown 15.00-15.28; street 3D 15.41-15.49; detail 15.85-16.03.
Excluded: Toole Park pins in frame 2 (clipped at the edge); Bess Reed pairs (short, park-centroid sensitive); courthouse icon (not detected).

Palette: 8-colour median-cut of the map area below the nav bar; pins by colour blob; purple pin needed a relaxed saturation threshold. Frame 6 city dots are hollow rings (about 12 px); centres are ring box centres.
Naming: 02 is the highest zoom; 01 is named for extruded buildings by visual judgement (not measured); 03 is the widest downtown frame. Owner order 2,3,1 became 01,02,03.
Status-bar times: frames 2-6 show 8:43 and frame 1 shows 8:44; the set may be a zoom-in run (inference only).
No user-placed points are visible in any frame (visual check).
WebFetch returns tool-summarised excerpts with no status or byte counts; quotes need a verbatim check before legal reliance; the Apple result covers only the clauses quoted.
Nominatim: 23 searches, 1.2 s apart (policy: at most 1 per second). Raw JSON and scripts are in the session scratchpad, not committed.
PIL 12.3.0 and numpy 2.5.3 were preinstalled; nothing pip-installed. Terrain, GIBS, GOES and MRMS availability comes from README s3 and was not re-checked.
